body.statement:
Let \(\delta_n=2^{-p_n-1}\), and, on \(\kappa_n=0\), let \(\mathcal B_n\) be the coordinate box of radius \(\delta_n\) about \((\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C)\). The certificate in \(H_n^{\mathrm{cert}}\) can be chosen so that there are finite constants \(K_\star\) and \(k_\star\), depending only on \(c,C_0,B,\sigma,r_0\), for which the following holds for all sufficiently large \(n>r_0\). If every coordinate of the box is at most \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1\) in absolute value, then
\[
0\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}
\le K_\star(n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+1)^{k_\star}.
\]
If in addition every donor matrix \(X'\) in the box satisfies
\[
s_r(X')\ge3cn/4,\qquad s_{r+1}(X')\le cn/4,
\qquad s_1(X')\le3C_0n/2,
\]
then
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}
\le K_\star(n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+1)^{k_\star}
\bigl(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n}\bigr).
\]
Every nonnegative radius recorded as a summand of either \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) or \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\) obeys the corresponding upper bound.
body.proof_tex:
The coarse bound in the proof of the deterministic certificate gives the first inequality. Indeed, with \(T=T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1\), the displayed bounds for \(\overline t,\overline R,\overline W,\overline d\), and \(\overline H\) are bounded by a fixed polynomial in \(n,T,\alpha^{-1}+1\); logarithms and square roots are bounded by one plus their arguments. The fallback radius \(M_0=B^2/c\) is fixed. The certificate never needs to record a radius larger than the diameter of the resulting coarse hull plus one final rounding unit. This proves the global polynomial bound.

For the sharp bound, set \(\tau=(cn/2)^2\). The assumed singular-value inequalities give, for both \(X'^{\top}X'\) and \(X'X'^{\top}\), a separation from \(\tau\) of at least
\[
\min\left\{(3cn/4)^2-(cn/2)^2,
(cn/2)^2-(cn/4)^2\right\}
=\frac{3c^2n^2}{16}.
\tag{4}
\]
For two matrices \(X_1,X_2\) in the box,
\[
\|X_1^{\top}X_1-X_2^{\top}X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le(\|X_1\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}})
\|X_1-X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K n\|X_1-X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{5}
\]
Let \(\Gamma\) be a rectangular contour lying in the gap (4) and enclosing the retained squared singular values. The resolvent identity gives
\[
P_R(X_1)-P_R(X_2)
=\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm i}\int_\Gamma
(z-X_1^{\top}X_1)^{-1}
(X_1^{\top}X_1-X_2^{\top}X_2)
(z-X_2^{\top}X_2)^{-1}\,dz.
\]
The contour has length \(O(n^2)\), while both resolvents are \(O(n^{-2})\) by (4). Combining this fact with (5) yields
\[
\|P_R(X_1)-P_R(X_2)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K\frac{\|X_1-X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n}.
\tag{6}
\]
The same bound holds for \(P_L\). Applying the ordinary inverse identity
\[
K_1^{-1}-K_2^{-1}=K_1^{-1}(K_2-K_1)K_2^{-1}
\]
to formula (1) in the preceding proof, using \(s_r(X_j)\ge3cn/4\), gives
\[
\|X_{1,r}^+-X_{2,r}^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K\frac{\|X_1-X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n^2}.
\tag{7}
\]
These derivations use a projector onto the entire retained cluster and therefore do not require distinct retained singular values.

Across the coordinate box,
\[
\|X_1-X_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2n\delta_n,qquad
\|R_1-R_2\|_2\le2\sqrt n\delta_n,qquad
\|C_1-C_2\|_2\le2\sqrt n\delta_n.
\tag{8}
\]
The invariant formulas
\[
RX_r^+C,quad \|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}},quad
\sigma^{-1}\sqrt{\|X_r^+C\|_2^2+\|(X_r^+)^{\top}R^{\top}\|_2^2},
\quad \|P_RR^{\top}\|_2/\sigma,quad \|P_LC\|_2/\sigma
\]
together with (6)--(8) show that their total variation over the box is at most
\[
K(n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1)^k2^{-p_n}
\]
for fixed \(K,k\). On the stable set,
\[
\frac{2}{3C_0n}\le\|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\frac{4}{3cn},
\]
so division by \(h_n=\|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) introduces only a polynomial factor. The arguments of every logarithm and square root in \(W_n\) are bounded away from zero. The derivative of \(\zeta_\alpha\) is also polynomially bounded in \(\alpha^{-1}\): if \(z=\Phi^{-1}(1-q)\) with \(3\alpha/8\le q\le\alpha/2\), then
\[
q=\int_z^\infty\phi(x)\,dx\le\frac{\phi(z)}{z},
\]
and \(z\) is bounded away from zero because \(q<1/4\). Hence \(1/\phi(z)\le K/\alpha\). The maps \(x\mapsto\max\{0,x\}\) and \(x\mapsto\|x\|_2\) are one-Lipschitz. It follows by composition that the encoding contribution is bounded by
\[
K_\star(n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+1)^{k_\star}2^{-p_n}.
\]

In directed \(q_n\)-bit arithmetic, a polynomial number of operations contributes at most a polynomial condition factor times \(2^{1-q_n}\). The residual tests for the matrix-sign and inverse steps are uniformly successful under (4), and the scalar quantile bisections have the positive-density bounds established in the deterministic proof. Therefore the arithmetic contribution is bounded by
\[
K_\star(n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+1)^{k_\star}2^{1-q_n}.
\]
Increasing \(K_\star,k_\star\) once gives the asserted sum. Since all recorded radii are nonnegative and their sum is \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\), each individual summand satisfies the same bound.
